notes: The shield is stacked on the Uno's headers. I made joined and electrical edges for the shield pins the tutorial uses: channel A D12/D3/D9/A0, channel B D13/D11/D8/A1, plus GND and VIN. Only channel A is driven in the sketch.
The motor goes on channel A (orange lead to A+, black lead to A-), as in the image. The motor is not polarised, so swapping the leads only reverses direction.

The battery holder's orange lead goes to the VIN screw terminal and its black lead to GND. Two 3.7 V cells in series give about 7.4 V, which is inside the shield's 5-12 V range and the motor's 6-12 V range.
The shield's VIN terminal also feeds the Uno's VIN pin through the stacked header. I recorded that as a stacked-pin edge.
The USB cable joins the Uno to the computer. The catalogue has no named USB port on the Uno, so the edge has no ports. The computer is not modelled.
No breadboard or jumper wires are used, because the leads go straight into the screw terminals.
